analysis:
The supplied units are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md lines 480-1150 (unchanged context) and the docs/provider/cli-reference.md patch. I found no changed executable code, so no concrete regression is demonstrable.

The documented changes describe behavior that exists in unsupplied source:
- cli-reference.md head line 1578 adds `~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json` (`VerifiedWeightHashStore`, mode 0600). It stores managed GLM load hashes bound to file identities, which startup registration reuses.
- The test.md patch excerpt (outside the numbered units) says the load reports a manifest aggregate only after every file verified, and that `ProviderLoop.ensureModelLoaded` runs no separate load-time `WeightHasher` pass.
- cli-reference.md head line 52 adds variable-frame-rate video support (video decode path).
- cli-reference.md head line 1604 changes the memory-admission text to count reclaimable file page cache as available.

The weight-hash change touches T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution) and A-004. It also touches the coordinator's weight-hash verification. The security question is whether a cached hash keyed on file identity (size, mtime or inode) can be reused after an operator swaps weights while preserving that identity. A related question is whether the store file is trusted and tamper-resistant against ADV-001, who has local write access. Another is whether the aggregate is bound to the manifest and revision. None of `VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift`, `ProviderLoop` or the GLM loader was supplied, so I cannot confirm or refute this.

The changed page-cache accounting in the memory-admission description may affect T-029 and availability. It is only a doc statement here. The variable-frame-rate video decode may widen the T-050/decoder attack surface, but the implementation is not visible.

Next pass should inspect VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift, the GLM load verification path, the video decoder, and the memory-availability code. The remaining test.md text (480-1150) is unchanged context and raised nothing.
